name: AGRITOX
label: AGRITOX
creator: INRA; ANSES
description: French database of pesticide active substances, created by INRA and now run by ANSES. It holds expert-validated data from regulatory dossiers and the literature: identity, physicochemical properties, acute toxicity, reference values (ADI, ARfD, AOEL), ecotoxicity and classification. The data are released as open files, so regulatory pesticide hazard data can be reused.

name: Australian Industrial Chemicals Introduction Scheme
label: AICIS
creator: AICIS (Australian Government)
description: Online database search portal of Australia's industrial chemicals regulator, which replaced NICNAS in July 2020. It gives access to the Australian Inventory of Industrial Chemicals, published human-health and environmental hazard, exposure and risk assessments (including reports inherited from NICNAS) and risk-management recommendations.

name: Nanosafety FAIR maturity indicators (Ammar et al.)
label: Nanosafety FAIR maturity indicators…
aliases: Ammar Ammar nanotox fair maturity indicators; 281 maturity indicators; FAIR maturity models/framework for Toxicology; FAIR assessment of nanosafety data reusability with community standards
creator: Maastricht University (BiGCaT)
description: These are machine-readable FAIR maturity indicators derived from twelve nanosafety minimum reporting standards. The NSDRA framework uses them to annotate nanosafety datasets and score how reusable the datasets are for specific computational risk assessment use cases.

name: Event Components (structured Key Event annotation)
label: Event Components
creator: US EPA; EC JRC
description: A structured way of describing each AOP Key Event as a biological process, a biological object and an action, each term taken from an existing ontology or controlled vocabulary. Implemented in the AOP-Wiki, it makes Key Events machine-readable so AOPs can be searched, compared and linked computationally.

name: AOP-DB (Adverse Outcome Pathway Database)
label: AOP-DB
creator: US EPA
description: The US EPA Adverse Outcome Pathway Database (AOP-DB) links AOP information from the AOP-Wiki to public data on genes, chemicals, diseases, pathways, species orthology and ToxCast assays. It supports computational exploration of the molecular targets and biological context of AOPs; this row covers the first version, described in 2018.

name: AOP-DB 2021 update (version 2)
label: second version of AOP-DB
aliases: second version of AOP-DB; aopdb2021; The 2021 update of the EPA's adverse outcome pathway database
creator: US EPA
description: Version 2 of the EPA AOP-DB (2021 update) added automated AOP-Wiki data pulls, tissue-, individual- and population-level gene data, semantic mapping with a SPARQL endpoint, and the first public web interface. The full database was also released as downloadable SQL files.

name: AOP-DB RDF
label: AOP-DB RDF
creator: US EPA; Maastricht University (BiGCaT)
description: AOP-DB RDF is a semantic-web (RDF) version of selected AOP-DB tables, mapped to ontologies and aligned with AOP-Wiki RDF, and served through a public SPARQL endpoint. It allows federated queries that link AOP data with genes, diseases, pathways and ToxCast assays.

name: AOP-helpFinder
label: AOP-helpFinder
creator: Universite Paris Cite / Inserm
description: AOP-helpFinder is a web tool with open code that text-mines PubMed abstracts. It finds where chemical stressors and biological events (molecular initiating events, key events, adverse outcomes) are mentioned together, so researchers can collect literature evidence to build and weigh adverse outcome pathways.

name: AOP-helpFinder 3.0
label: AOP-helpFinder 3.0
creator: Universite Paris Cite / Inserm
description: AOP-helpFinder 3.0 is the third major version of AOP-helpFinder. It adds network views of the stressor-event and event-event (key event relationship) links found by text mining, and annotates them with data from external sources such as AOP-Wiki, KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome, UniProt and disease-gene databases.

name: OECD Adverse Outcome Pathway Knowledge Base (AOP-KB)
label: AOP-KB
creator: OECD (with US EPA, EC JRC and US Army ERDC)
description: The OECD Adverse Outcome Pathway Knowledge Base (AOP-KB) is the OECD web platform that brings together tools for developing, reviewing and sharing adverse outcome pathways. The AOP-Wiki is its core module, alongside Effectopedia, AOP Xplorer and the Intermediate Effects DB. Since mid-2026 its address redirects to the AOP-Wiki.

name: AOP-networkFinder
label: AOP-networkFinder
creator: Norwegian Institute of Public Health (FHI); University of Oslo
description: AOP-networkFinder is a web application, also available as open code and a Docker image. It pulls content from AOP-Wiki to build, merge, annotate and visualise networks of adverse outcome pathways, and exports them to Cytoscape for further analysis.

name: AOP Ontology (AOPO)
label: AOP Ontology (AOPO)
creator: US Army ERDC (L. Burgoon)
description: An OWL ontology for adverse outcome pathways that reuses classes from existing biomedical ontologies to describe molecular initiating events, key events and adverse outcomes in a common vocabulary. It enables computational reasoning over AOPs, and its terms are reused, for example, in the AOP-Wiki RDF.

name: AOP-Wiki
label: AOP-Wiki
subdomains: AOP-based mechanistic knowledge; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: OECD (with US EPA and EC JRC)
description: The AOP-Wiki is the OECD collaborative wiki for building, reviewing and publishing adverse outcome pathways. It records molecular initiating events, key events, key event relationships, stressors and the supporting evidence in a structured template. Its downloadable content is the central reference store of AOP knowledge for regulatory and computational toxicology.

name: AOP-Wiki RDF
label: AOP-Wiki RDF
creator: Maastricht University (BiGCaT)
description: A Linked Data version of the AOP-Wiki, converted from the AOP-Wiki XML export into RDF and served through a public SPARQL endpoint. It maps AOPs, key events and stressors to external gene, protein and chemical identifiers, so AOP knowledge can be queried and combined with other resources.

name: The Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority (APVMA) database of completed chemical reviews
label: APVMA-CR
creator: APVMA
description: Listing of chemical reviews by the Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority: completed, ongoing and scheduled reconsiderations of registered agricultural and veterinary chemicals. Review reports document human-health, environmental, residue and worker-safety assessments and the resulting regulatory decisions.

name: ArrayExpress
label: ArrayExpress
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: Public EMBL-EBI archive for functional genomics experiments, mainly gene expression data from microarrays and high-throughput sequencing (including single-cell), annotated to MIAME and MINSEQE. Now served through BioStudies but with its own data model and Annotare submission tool, it lets toxicogenomics datasets be deposited, found and reused.

name: ArrayTrack
label: ArrayTrack
creator: US FDA NCTR
description: ArrayTrack is FDA NCTR software that combines a MIAME-supportive microarray database, local copies of public annotation libraries and analysis tools. It was used to store, analyse and interpret toxicogenomics and pharmacogenomics data, including genomic data submitted to FDA.

name: BioAssay Ontology (BAO)
label: BioAssay Ontology (BAO)
creator: University of Miami
description: The BioAssay Ontology (BAO) is an OWL ontology that describes biological screening assays and their results, including assay format, design, detection technology, target and endpoint. It allows bioassay and high-throughput screening data (for example from PubChem) to be annotated consistently, queried and integrated.

name: BioModels
label: BioModels
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: A repository of mathematical models of biological processes taken from the literature, many of them manually curated, annotated and checked for reproducibility, mostly in SBML. Models get stable identifiers and semantic annotations, so they can be found, cited, simulated and reused, including in quantitative systems toxicology and PBK modelling.

name: Bioschemas ChemicalSubstance Profile
label: Bioschemas ChemicalSubstance Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: Bioschemas profile that sets out which schema.org properties (identifiers, names, composition, links to ChEBI and other ontology terms) to use when marking up web pages about chemical substances. Substance records on websites and databases then become findable by search engines and harvesters and interoperable as structured metadata.

name: Bioschemas ComputationalTool Profile
label: Bioschemas ComputationalTool Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: Bioschemas profile for describing software tools and services with schema.org markup: name, function, inputs and outputs, version, operating system, licence and citation, using EDAM terms as in bio.tools. It makes research software, including in silico toxicology tools, findable and comparable on the web.

name: Bioschemas ComputationalWorkflow Profile
label: Bioschemas ComputationalWorkflow Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: Bioschemas profile that defines schema.org metadata for computational workflows (creators, workflow language, inputs and outputs as formal parameters, licence, version), so that workflows can be described, found and cited, for example in WorkflowHub and Workflow RO-Crate. It supports FAIR sharing of analysis pipelines, including those used in toxicology.

name: Bioschemas Dataset Profile
label: Bioschemas Dataset Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: A Bioschemas profile that sets out which schema.org Dataset properties life-science data providers should embed in their dataset web pages, graded as minimum, recommended or optional. Consistent markup lets search engines, registries and portals harvest dataset descriptions, so datasets are easier to find across repositories.

name: Bioschemas MolecularEntity Profile
label: Bioschemas MolecularEntity Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: A Bioschemas profile for describing chemical entities such as molecules, ions or complexes on web pages with schema.org properties (names, identifiers, InChI, InChIKey, SMILES, molecular formula). Chemical records on different sites can then be harvested and linked through shared structured metadata.

name: Bioschemas Sample Profile
label: Bioschemas Sample Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: A Bioschemas profile with a minimal set of schema.org properties, plus Bioschemas extensions, to identify, link and describe biological samples on web pages. Biobanks and sample databases can then expose comparable sample metadata that search engines and aggregators can harvest.

name: BioSamples
label: BioSamples
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: EMBL-EBI database that stores and curates metadata about biological samples used in assays and gives each one a stable accession. A sample can be described once and then linked to data in archives such as ENA, ArrayExpress and PRIDE, so omics data can be searched and combined across databases by sample characteristics.

name: BioStudies
label: BioStudies
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: An EMBL-EBI archive for whole biological studies. It stores study-level metadata, links to data held in other archives, and data files that have no dedicated repository. It hosts project collections, including those of toxicology projects, and now holds the ArrayExpress functional genomics data.

name: Biocides in the environment
label: Biocides in the environment
creator: German Environment Agency (UBA)
description: Database of the German Environment Agency on the ChemInfo platform. It collects monitoring data on biocidal active substances in water, wastewater, soil, sediment, sewage sludge and biota from Germany, Austria and Switzerland, together with approval status, physicochemical properties and CLP classification. Environmental occurrence data for biocides can be searched and exported.

name: The Blood Exposome Database
label: The Blood Exposome Database
creator: UC Davis (West Coast Metabolomics Center)
description: Database of chemicals reported in human blood. It was built by text-mining PubMed and PubChem and merging chemical lists from metabolomics, exposure science, toxicology and nutrition. It supports exposome research and the annotation of untargeted metabolomics and exposomics data.

name: CAS Registry Number
label: CAS Registry Number
creator: CAS (Chemical Abstracts Service), American Chemical Society
description: Numeric identifier, up to ten digits in three hyphenated parts ending in a check digit, that CAS assigns to each distinct substance in its CAS REGISTRY. It is the most widely used substance identifier in chemical inventories, regulations and safety data, and links names and data across sources.

name: Canada’s Existing Substances Assessment Repository
label: CESAR
creator: Environment and Climate Change Canada; Health Canada
description: Canadian repository of risk and other regulatory assessment reports on existing substances under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, from the Priority Substances List and the Chemicals Management Plan. Each report covers substance identity, exposure, effects and risk characterisation. Reports are reached through eChemPortal and Health Canada's chemical substances portal.

name: ChEBI (Chemical Entities of Biological Interest)
label: ChEBI
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: ChEBI (Chemical Entities of Biological Interest) is a freely available dictionary and ontology of small molecular entities, classified by chemical structure and by biological or application role. Its stable identifiers, names, structures and cross-references are widely used to annotate chemicals in databases and ontologies.

name: ChEMBL
label: ChEMBL
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: Open, manually curated database of bioactive, drug-like molecules that links chemical structures to bioactivity measurements, assays and targets, mostly extracted from the medicinal chemistry literature. Its standardised, downloadable data support in silico modelling, including of off-target and toxicity-related activities.

name: ChemInfo
label: ChemInfo
creator: German federal and Länder authorities (ChemInfo cooperation, UBA)
description: Chemical information system run jointly by the German federal and state authorities as the successor of the GSBL substance data pool. For each substance it compiles identity, physicochemical, toxicological and ecotoxicological data, environmental occurrence, hazard and emergency-response information and the relevant legal provisions. A public subset can be searched without registration; the full data set is open to authorities and emergency services.

name: ChemSpider
label: ChemSpider
creator: ChemZoo; Royal Society of Chemistry
description: Free chemical structure database, now run by the Royal Society of Chemistry. It merges compounds from hundreds of data sources into structure-based records with names, identifiers, properties and links back to the sources. It helps resolve chemical identity and locate data on a substance.

name: Cell Ontology (CL)
label: Cell Ontology (CL)
creator: Cell Ontology community (OBO Foundry); originally Univ. of Edinburgh, Carnegie Institution, Univ. of Cambridge
description: The Cell Ontology (CL) is an OBO Foundry ontology of cell types across organisms, with definitions and links to anatomy and other ontologies. It gives standard terms for annotating the cell types used in experiments and recorded in datasets.

name: COMBINE FAIRsharing collection
label: COMBINE FAIRsharing collection
creator: COMBINE (with FAIRsharing)
description: A FAIRsharing collection, maintained with the COMBINE network, that groups the community standards for computational modelling in biology (e.g. SBML, CellML, SED-ML, SBGN and the COMBINE archive format) with related resources. It gives modellers one curated entry point to interoperable formats for exchanging, annotating and simulating models.

name: EPA CompTox Chemicals Dashboard
label: EPA CompTox Chemicals Dashboard
subdomains: in vitro toxicology; exposome; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: US EPA
description: US EPA web application built on the curated DSSTox substance and structure database. For about a million chemicals it brings together physicochemical, fate, exposure, use, in vivo toxicity and ToxCast/Tox21 in vitro bioactivity data. Batch search, identifier mapping and downloads make these data reusable for computational toxicology and risk assessment.

name: FAIR Cookbook
label: FAIR Cookbook
creator: FAIRplus / ELIXIR
description: An open online collection of practical recipes that show step by step how to make life-science data findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable. Topics include identifiers, metadata, vocabularies, licensing and FAIRness assessment. Domain experts write and review the recipes, and communities, including toxicology, can add their own.

name: Cosmetic ingredient database
label: Cosmetic ingredient database
creator: European Commission (DG GROW)
description: European Commission information database on cosmetic substances and ingredients. It gives INCI names, CAS/EC numbers, functions and regulatory status under EU cosmetics law (annex entries and restrictions back to 1976), with links to scientific committee opinions. It has no legal value, but it makes the regulatory status of an ingredient easy to find.

name: CRED (Criteria for Reporting and Evaluating ecotoxicity Data)
label: CRED
creator: Swiss Ecotox Centre; RIVM; Stockholm University
description: A method for evaluating the reliability (20 criteria) and relevance (13 criteria) of aquatic ecotoxicity studies, with reporting recommendations and an Excel evaluation tool. It makes study evaluations transparent and consistent, so peer-reviewed ecotoxicity data can be reused in regulatory hazard and risk assessment.

name: Comparative Toxicogenomics Database
label: CTD
creator: MDI Biological Laboratory; NC State University
description: Public knowledgebase in which biocurators extract chemical-gene, chemical-disease, gene-disease and chemical exposure relationships from the literature. These are integrated with external data such as GO and pathways to infer chemical-gene-disease networks. It helps generate hypotheses on how environmental chemicals affect human health.

name: Danish (Q)SAR Database
label: Danish (Q)SAR Database
subdomains: computational and predictive toxicology; regulatory toxicology
creator: DTU National Food Institute (first version from the Danish EPA QSAR group, with ECB support)
description: Searchable database of (Q)SAR predictions for a large inventory of chemicals. It covers physicochemical, environmental fate, ecotoxicity, ADME and human health endpoints, uses commercial, free and DTU-built models, and documents each model in QMRF format. It is used to screen and prioritise chemicals and to support classification in chemical regulation.

name: DC Data Explorer
label: DC Data Explorer
creator: Douglas Connect (now Edelweiss Connect)
description: DC Data Explorer is a Douglas Connect web interface with REST APIs. It gives harmonised programmatic access to the US EPA ToxCast/Tox21 and ToxRefDB data and to the Open TG-GATEs toxicogenomics data, so users can search across these sources and pull the data into workflow tools.

name: diXa data infrastructure for chemical safety assessment
label: diXa
stakeholders: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
creator: diXa consortium (Maastricht University, EMBL-EBI)
description: A data infrastructure from the EU FP7 diXa project that connected a central toxicogenomics data warehouse at EMBL-EBI to a portal linking chemical, molecular and phenotype information. It offered online templates and guidelines for depositing data, plus tools for analysing them; the service is no longer online.

name: DrugBank
label: DrugBank
creator: University of Alberta (Wishart lab); OMx Personal Health Analytics
description: Bioinformatics and cheminformatics knowledgebase that combines detailed drug data (chemistry, pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, toxicity) with information on drug targets, enzymes and transporters. It is free for academic use and supports drug discovery and computational studies of drug safety.

name: Dietary Supplement Label Database
label: DSLD
creator: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements (ODS) and National Library of Medicine (NLM)
description: Public NIH database of the full label content of dietary supplement products sold in the United States (ingredients and amounts, claims, warnings and label images) for current and historical products, searchable online and downloadable through an API. It supports research on supplement composition and exposure, including screening for potentially harmful ingredients.

name: EC Inventory
label: EC Inventory
creator: European Commission (JRC); ECHA
description: Combined EU list of EINECS (substances on the market between 1971 and 1981), ELINCS (notified new substances) and the No-Longer-Polymers list, now maintained by ECHA. It assigns the EC numbers that identify substances in EU chemicals legislation and provides reference names for regulatory submissions.

name: ECHA Biocidal Products Regulation
label: ECHA-BPR
creator: ECHA
description: ECHA database of biocidal active substances, organised by active substance and product type. For each it shows approval status under the Biocidal Products Regulation, whether it is a candidate for substitution, and links to assessment reports and authorised products. It makes the outcome of EU biocide evaluations publicly accessible.

name: ECHA CHEM - Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals Regulation
label: ECHA CHEM - REACH
creator: ECHA
description: ECHA's public chemicals database. Its first release published the non-confidential content of all REACH registration dossiers: substance identity, physicochemical, toxicological and ecotoxicological data and safe-use information. It is gradually absorbing ECHA's other public chemical data, such as the C&L Inventory.

name: ECHA Classification, Labelling and Packaging
label: ECHA-CLP
creator: ECHA
description: Public EU database of classification and labelling information on substances notified or registered under the CLP and REACH Regulations. It includes industry self-classifications and the harmonised classifications of CLP Annex VI. The stand-alone database opened in 2012 and has been replaced by the C&L Inventory in ECHA CHEM.

name: OECD eChemPortal
label: OECD eChemPortal
creator: OECD
description: OECD global portal that searches many national, regional and international government chemical databases at once. It returns physicochemical, fate, ecotoxicity and toxicity data, hazard and risk assessments and GHS classifications, with direct links to the source records.

name: ECOTOXicology Knowledgebase
label: ECOTOXicology Knowledgebase
creator: US EPA
description: US EPA knowledgebase of curated single-chemical toxicity test results for aquatic organisms, terrestrial plants and wildlife, taken from the literature and coded with controlled vocabularies. Its searchable, downloadable records, linked to other chemical resources, support ecological risk assessment, water-quality criteria and model development.

name: Ecotoxicology thesaurus
label: Ecotoxicology thesaurus
creator: INIST-CNRS
description: A bilingual French-English SKOS thesaurus of about 4,700 ecotoxicology concepts, published by INIST-CNRS on the Loterre platform. It covers pollutants and their effects on ecosystems and human health, as well as organisms, places and chemical compounds. It provides controlled, linkable terms with synonyms for indexing and searching ecotoxicology literature and data.

name: EdelweissData
label: EdelweissData
creator: Edelweiss Connect
description: A data management and publishing platform from Edelweiss Connect that ingests, annotates, harmonises and versions tabular datasets and serves them through a web interface and a query API. Its public instance hosts toxicology-related datasets, including in vitro and QSAR data.

name: EFSA statement on the interpretation of FAIR principles for mechanistic effect models in the regulatory environmental risk assessment of pesticides
label: EFSA FAIR statement
aliases: EFSA FAIR statement; EFSA FAIR statement for mechanistic effect models
subdomains: eco-toxicology; computational and predictive toxicology; regulatory toxicology
creator: EFSA
description: This EFSA statement interprets the FAIR principles for mechanistic effect models used in the environmental risk assessment of pesticides. It covers the underlying data, the model code and the model assessment, lists supporting resources, and gives recommendations for putting the principles into practice.

name: ELIXIR Deposition Databases
label: ELIXIR Deposition Databases
creator: ELIXIR
description: ELIXIR's list of recommended repositories for depositing experimental life-science data, chosen against technical-quality and governance criteria in line with the FAIR principles. It points researchers, funders and publishers to suitable archives (e.g. ENA, ArrayExpress/BioStudies, PRIDE, MetaboLights, BioModels) for publishing open data.

name: eNanoMapper database
label: eNanoMapper database
creator: eNanoMapper consortium (Ideaconsult)
description: A public database, built by Ideaconsult on its AMBIT software within the eNanoMapper project, that holds nanomaterial characterisation data together with biological and toxicological study results. Data can be uploaded via configurable spreadsheet templates, searched, and downloaded in several standard formats through a web interface and REST API.

name: eNanoMapper ontology
label: eNanoMapper ontology
creator: eNanoMapper consortium (EMBL-EBI, Maastricht University)
description: An OWL ontology for nanomaterial safety that assembles slimmed modules from existing ontologies such as ChEBI, NPO, BAO and OBI and adds nano-specific classes. It supplies the shared vocabulary for annotating nanomaterials, their characterisation and toxicity assays in eNanoMapper-based databases.

name: Ensembl
label: Ensembl
creator: EMBL-EBI and Wellcome Sanger Institute
description: Genome database and browser that produces and distributes reference genome assemblies, gene and transcript annotation with stable identifiers, comparative genomics, variation and regulatory data for vertebrates and other eukaryotes, through the web, APIs and bulk downloads. Toxicology uses it to map, identify and annotate genes in omics data.

name: Environment Ontology
label: Environment Ontology
creator: EnvO Consortium (from the Genomic Standards Consortium)
description: An OBO Foundry ontology of environments: biomes, environmental features and systems, environmental materials and processes. Its terms annotate where organisms and samples come from, so environmental metadata can be integrated and searched across databases.

name: EPA Aquatic Life Benchmarks
label: EPA Aquatic Life Benchmarks
creator: US EPA (Office of Pesticide Programs)
description: Table from EPA's Office of Pesticide Programs giving freshwater toxicity benchmarks for registered pesticides and their degradates: acute and chronic values for fish, invertebrates and plants. Each value links to the EPA risk assessment it comes from, with Office of Water criteria shown where they exist. States, tribes and others use it to interpret pesticide levels measured in water and to decide which sites to follow up.

name: EPA ChemView
label: EPA ChemView
creator: US EPA (Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention)
description: US EPA web database that brings together, per chemical, health and safety data submitted under the Toxic Substances Control Act and EPA's own assessments and regulatory actions (such as significant new use rules), with summary templates, links to source documents and export. It makes non-confidential TSCA chemical information findable and reusable.

name: EPA Integrated Risk Information System
label: EPA IRIS
creator: US EPA
description: US EPA programme and database of chemical health hazard assessments. Each assessment has a peer-reviewed toxicological review and toxicity values such as oral reference doses, inhalation reference concentrations and cancer slope factors or unit risks. It gives agencies and others a consistent, citable source of human-health toxicity values for risk assessment.

name: EPA Substance Registry Services
label: EPA Substance Registry Services
creator: US EPA
description: EPA's central registry of the chemicals, biological organisms and other substances that EPA tracks or regulates. Each substance gets an EPA identifier with its names, synonyms and CAS number, and links to the EPA programmes, lists and regulations that cover it, so substances are identified the same way across EPA data systems.

name: Chromium Epigenomics Toxicology
label: EpiCrDB
creator: University of Cincinnati (Puga laboratory)
description: Small University of Cincinnati web portal giving FAIR access to epigenomics datasets (ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, MNase-seq, FAIRE) on how hexavalent chromium disturbs chromatin organisation. It adds curated chemical, cell, antibody and treatment metadata, with links to GEO, BioProject and PubMed.

name: eTRANSAFE guidelines for research reproducibility, FAIR data sharing and model verification
label: eTRANSAFE guidelines for research…
aliases: eTRANSAFE research reproducibility guidelines; eTRANSAFE: Building a sustainable framework to share reproducible drug safety knowledge with the public domain
subdomains: computational and predictive toxicology; regulatory toxicology
creator: eTRANSAFE consortium (IMI2)
description: Guidelines from the IMI2 eTRANSAFE project on research reproducibility in drug safety, made up of FAIR data-sharing guidelines and guidelines for verifying predictive models. They describe how public and proprietary preclinical and clinical safety data and models should be managed and shared so results can be reproduced and reused.

name: European Union Observatory for Nanomaterials
label: EUON
creator: ECHA (for the European Commission)
description: Observatory website hosted by ECHA that gives neutral public information, in all EU languages, on nanomaterials on the EU market: their uses, safety, regulation and research. It links to searchable nanomaterial data such as registered nanoforms and related databases and studies.

name: EU-ToxRisk Knowledge Portal (knowledge infrastructure)
label: EU-ToxRisk Knowledge Portal
aliases: EU-ToxRisk Knowledge Portal; EU-ToxRisk KI; modular knowledge infrastructure
creator: EU-ToxRisk consortium (Edelweiss Connect)
description: The data and knowledge management infrastructure of the EU-ToxRisk project. It combines a common data and metadata format, a methods database documenting test protocols, data archiving, an API for access to individual data points, analysis notebooks and a knowledge portal. It was built to make in vitro new approach method data from many laboratories documented, shareable and reusable for risk assessment.

name: Exposure Ontology
label: Exposure Ontology
creator: CTD team (NC State University) and US EPA
description: An exposure-science ontology built on four core concepts: exposure stressor, exposure receptor, exposure event and exposure outcome. It was developed with the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database and gives shared terms for capturing exposure data and linking them to toxicology, epidemiology and health data.

name: Exposome Explorer
label: Exposome Explorer
creator: IARC (WHO)
description: Manually curated IARC database of biomarkers of exposure to dietary and environmental risk factors. It records measured concentrations in human biospecimens, the study populations and analytical methods, correlations with external exposure measures, and reproducibility over time. Researchers use it to choose and compare exposure biomarkers for exposome and epidemiological studies.

name: Reference AOP FAIR Implementation Profile
label: Reference AOP FIP
creator: FAIR-AOPs community (GO FAIR Foundation, EC JRC, US EPA)
description: This is the reference FAIR Implementation Profile for adverse outcome pathways. It records which FAIR-enabling resources (identifiers, vocabularies, formats, repositories, licences) the FAIR-AOPs community recommends for each FAIR principle, published as machine-readable nanopublications through the FIP Wizard.

name: FAIR Connect
label: FAIR Connect
creator: GO FAIR Foundation and IOS Press (now Sage), with CODATA, DTL and Health-RI
description: An open-access platform for FAIR data stewardship where FAIR-supporting resources, FAIR Implementation Profiles and community good practices are published, searched and discussed. It links the human-readable descriptions in the FAIR Connect journal to their machine-readable nanopublications and offers a search engine and dashboard over them.

name: FAIRsharing
label: FAIRsharing
creator: University of Oxford (FAIRsharing team)
description: A curated registry covering all disciplines that lists data and metadata standards, databases and repositories, data policies and collections. The records link to each other and each carries a DOI. It helps researchers, publishers and funders find, choose and cite suitable standards and repositories, and it gives FAIR assessment tools machine-readable descriptions of these resources.

name: FIP Wizard
label: FIP Wizard
creator: GO FAIR Foundation / Data Stewardship Wizard team (CTU Prague)
description: A web application built on the Data Stewardship Wizard that guides a community through the FIP questionnaire to declare its FAIR implementation choices for each principle. It publishes the resulting FAIR Implementation Profiles, and any newly declared FAIR-enabling resources, as machine-actionable nanopublications.

name: FIP Matrix tool
label: FIP Matrix tool
aliases: FIP convergence matrix; FAIR Convergence Matrix
creator: GO FAIR
description: The GO FAIR FAIR Convergence Matrix: an online questionnaire platform in which communities of practice record, principle by principle, the standards, vocabularies and services they use to implement FAIR. The answers form their FAIR Implementation Profiles. Combining these choices shows where communities converge, so others can reuse proven FAIR implementation options.

name: FAIR Implementation Profile (FIP)
label: FIP
creator: GO FAIR Foundation
description: A FAIR Implementation Profile lists, principle by principle, the FAIR-enabling resources (standards, vocabularies, identifier schemes, repositories, licences) that a community of practice has chosen. FIPs are published as machine-actionable nanopublications, so communities can document, compare and reuse each other's choices and move towards interoperable solutions.

name: Food and Feed Information Portal Database
label: Food and Feed Information Portal…
creator: European Commission (DG SANTE)
description: European Commission portal that brings together EU databases on authorised food and feed substances and products. It covers food additives, enzymes, flavourings and smoke flavourings, feed additives, food contact materials, novel foods, GMOs and health claims, with their authorisation status and conditions of use.

name: F-UJI
label: F-UJI
aliases: F-UJI automated FAIR assessment tool; FUIJ
creator: PANGAEA (FAIRsFAIR)
description: An open-source web service and API that automatically assesses how FAIR a published dataset is, starting from its persistent identifier and applying the FAIRsFAIR data object assessment metrics. It reports scores and test results for each FAIR principle, which repositories and data producers can use to improve their metadata.

name: OECD Guidance Document 211 (describing non-guideline in vitro test methods)
label: OECD Guidance Document 211
creator: OECD
description: OECD guidance with a harmonised template for describing non-guideline in vitro test methods, covering the test system, procedure, data interpretation and performance. It makes method metadata complete and consistent, so regulators can judge whether data from such methods can be used in assessments.

name: OECD Guidance Document on the Generation, Reporting and Use of Research Data for Regulatory Assessments
label: OECD research data guidance
aliases: OECD research data guidance; OECD Guidance Document on research data
creator: OECD
description: OECD guidance on how research data, for example from academic studies that do not follow test guidelines, should be generated, reported and evaluated so they can be used in regulatory chemical assessments. It sets expectations for documentation and data availability that make such data reusable by regulators.

name: Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO)
label: GEO
creator: NCBI
description: NCBI's public archive for high-throughput functional genomics data, mostly microarray and sequencing-based gene expression studies. It stores raw and processed data with MIAME-oriented descriptions under stable accessions, so toxicogenomics datasets can be retrieved and reanalysed.

name: NITE Japan-GHS
label: NITE Japan-GHS
creator: NITE (National Institute of Technology and Evaluation, Japan)
description: NITE's consolidated database of the Japanese Government's GHS hazard classifications. For each substance it gives only the latest classification, with hazard categories, label elements and the rationale, as web pages and downloadable Excel lists in Japanese and English. It supports GHS labels and safety data sheets and the reuse of authoritative hazard classifications.

name: Gene Ontology (GO)
label: Gene Ontology (GO)
creator: Gene Ontology Consortium
description: The Gene Ontology (GO) is a structured vocabulary, independent of species, of molecular functions, biological processes and cellular components, used to annotate genes and gene products. It enables consistent functional annotation and enrichment analysis across organisms and databases.

name: HGNC gene symbols
label: HGNC gene symbols
creator: HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee
description: The approved symbols, names and stable identifiers that the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee assigns to human genes, served through genenames.org. They give each gene one unambiguous label across publications and databases, which is needed to link gene-level toxicology knowledge, such as AOP key events, to other resources.

name: ILO-WHO International Chemical Safety Cards
label: ICSCs
creator: ILO and WHO (IPCS), with the European Commission
description: Collection of standardised, peer-reviewed data sheets on chemicals, written in standard phrases. Each card gives identity, physical and chemical properties, health and environmental hazards, exposure limits, classification and protective measures; more than 1,700 cards exist in many languages. They give workplaces concise hazard information and can be searched in the ILO ICSC database.

name: Identifiers.org
label: Identifiers.org
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: Identifiers.org is an EMBL-EBI registry and resolver that gives life-science data collections a namespace prefix and resolves compact identifiers (prefix:accession) and identifiers.org URIs to the matching data record. It makes references to data stable, globally unique and resolvable, which supports the annotation of models and datasets.

name: IGS - Public Informationssystem für gefährliche Stoffe
label: IGS
creator: LANUK NRW (formerly LANUV / Landesumweltamt NRW), Germany
description: Public substance information system of the North Rhine-Westphalia environment agency. For each chemical or microbiological substance it compiles regulatory information from German, EU, Swiss, US and other legislation, together with physical-chemical, toxicological and emergency-response data. The public, authorities and emergency services use it to look up the legal status and hazards of substances.

name: InChI (IUPAC International Chemical Identifier)
label: InChIs
creator: IUPAC / NIST / InChI Trust
description: The IUPAC International Chemical Identifier (InChI) is an open algorithm and text string that encodes a chemical structure in a canonical, layered form; the hashed InChIKey is a fixed-length version for searching. It gives chemical substances a unique, machine-readable identifier, so chemical records can be linked and deduplicated across databases.

name: International Harmonization of Nomenclature and Diagnostic criteria
label: INHAND
creator: STP, ESTP, BSTP and JSTP (INHAND initiative)
description: An internationally harmonised nomenclature, with diagnostic criteria, for proliferative and non-proliferative lesions in laboratory animals. The toxicologic pathology societies publish it one organ system at a time, and it is maintained on the goRENI platform. It standardises how histopathology findings in non-clinical safety studies are recorded and supports the controlled terminology used for regulatory data exchange (SEND).

name: Integrated Effect Database for Toxicological Observations (INTOB)
label: INTOB
creator: UFZ Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (marketed by GREENBAY Software GmbH)
description: INTOB is a cloud-based data management application with an integrated database and a controlled vocabulary of effects. It records phenotypic observations and metadata from organism-level toxicity tests, mainly the zebrafish embryo acute toxicity test, so that results can be compared and reanalysed across studies.

name: Information Platform for Chemical Monitoring
label: IPCHEM
creator: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC)
description: European Commission platform, hosted by the JRC, for finding and accessing chemical monitoring data collections in four modules: environment, human biomonitoring, food and feed, and products and indoor air. Data come from EU bodies, Member States, international organisations and research projects. It harmonises and quality-checks occurrence data and offers one access point for exposure and risk assessment.

name: Internationally Peer Reviewed Chemical Safety Information
label: IPCS INCHEM
creator: WHO IPCS and CCOHS
description: Free portal from WHO's International Programme on Chemical Safety and the Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety. It gives searchable full-text access to internationally peer-reviewed chemical safety documents, including EHC monographs, CICADs, JECFA and JMPR evaluations, IARC summaries, ICSCs and poisons information monographs.

name: ISA-JSON
label: ISA-JSON
creator: ISA team, University of Oxford
description: ISA-JSON is the JSON serialisation of the ISA (Investigation-Study-Assay) metadata model, defined by JSON schemas and implemented in the ISA-API. It records study design, sample provenance, protocols and data files in machine-actionable form, so metadata can be validated, converted and submitted to repositories.

name: ISA framework (Investigation-Study-Assay; ISA-Tab)
label: ISA
subdomains: in vitro toxicology; nanotoxicology; exposome; toxicogenomics
creator: ISA team (EMBL-EBI, later University of Oxford)
description: The ISA framework is a general Investigation-Study-Assay metadata model, with ISA-Tab as its tab-delimited format and a set of supporting tools, for describing multi-omics and other life-science experiments. It records study design, sample characteristics, protocols and data files, so experimental metadata can be reported consistently, validated and reused.

name: IUCLID (International Uniform Chemical Information Database)
label: IUCLID
creator: European Commission JRC (ECB); since 2008 ECHA with OECD
description: IUCLID is free software for recording, storing, maintaining and exchanging data on the intrinsic and hazard properties of chemical substances. It implements the OECD Harmonised Templates and is the required format for dossiers under REACH, the Biocidal Products Regulation and other regulatory programmes.

name: IUPAC Glossary of terms used in immunotoxicology (IUPAC Recommendations 2012)
label: IUPAC immunotox glossary
creator: IUPAC
description: An IUPAC Recommendation that gives agreed definitions, with explanatory notes, for terms used in immunotoxicology. It supports consistent terminology when immunotoxicity data are reported and interpreted.

name: IUPAC Glossary of terms used in toxicology, 2nd edition (IUPAC Recommendations 2007)
label: IUPAC toxicology glossary
aliases: IUPAC toxicology glossary; Glossary Of Terms Used In Toxicology
creator: IUPAC
description: The second edition of IUPAC's glossary of toxicology, giving recommended definitions for terms used in toxicology and chemical risk assessment. It serves as a common reference vocabulary for consistent use of toxicological terms in data and publications.

name: Japan Chemicals Collaborative Knowledge database
label: J-CHECK
creator: NITE with MHLW, METI and MOE (Japan)
description: Japanese government database on substances covered by the Chemical Substances Control Law (CSCL). It gives the official substance lists and classes; test results on biodegradation, bioaccumulation, ecotoxicity and human toxicity from the existing-chemicals survey and the Japan Challenge Program; and risk assessment outcomes, in Japanese and English. It is linked to the OECD eChemPortal.

name: Japan Existing Chemical Database
label: JECDB
creator: NIHS (MHLW), Japan
description: Japanese database of toxicity test reports on existing chemicals tested in Japan's safety programme and in the OECD HPV programme, covering acute, repeated-dose, reproductive and developmental, genotoxicity and other tests. It gives English summaries, full reports in Japanese and IUCLID export files.

name: MARS (Multi-omics Adapter for Repository Submissions)
label: MARS
creator: ELIXIR (BioHackathon Europe; ELIXIR Data Platform)
description: MARS (Multi-omics Adapter for Repository Submissions) is an ELIXIR framework, with a command-line tool and repository adapters, for submitting a multi-omics study described in ISA-JSON to several public repositories (BioSamples, ENA, MetaboLights) in one go. It aims to keep metadata and accession numbers consistent across those repositories.

name: MDL Molfile Format
label: MDL Molfile Format
creator: MDL Information Systems (now Dassault Systemes BIOVIA)
description: A plain-text chemical file format from the CTfile family first published by MDL. It stores a molecule's atoms, bonds and coordinates as a connection table with optional property blocks (V2000 and V3000). Almost all cheminformatics software reads it, so it is a standard way to exchange structures, for example as input to QSAR and read-across tools.

name: MIAME (Minimum Information About a Microarray Experiment)
label: MIAME
creator: FGED (MGED) Society
description: MIAME is a reporting guideline that lists the minimum information needed to interpret and reproduce a microarray experiment: raw and processed data, sample annotation, experimental design, array design and protocols. It underlies the transcriptomics submission requirements of repositories such as GEO and ArrayExpress and of many journals.

name: Minimum Information about an array-based toxicogenomics experiment
label: MIAME/Tox
creator: ILSI HESI; EMBL-EBI; NIEHS (MGED)
description: An extension of MIAME that lists what to report with array-based toxicogenomics experiments, adding toxicology study design, treatments and conventional toxicity endpoints to the microarray description. It was meant to make toxicogenomics data comparable and ready for deposition in ArrayExpress (via Tox-MIAMExpress) and CEBS. It is no longer maintained.

name: Minimum Information about Animal Toxicology Experiments
label: MIATE
creator: Michigan State University (Zacharewski lab)
description: A community minimum-information checklist (MIATE/invivo) for the metadata of in vivo animal toxicology studies. It comes with recommended ontologies and templates for CEDAR, GEO, ISA and the Single Cell Portal. Labs can record study design and conditions in a standard form, so animal toxicology and toxicogenomics data can be found and reused.

name: MIRIAM (Minimum Information Requested in the Annotation of biochemical Models)
label: MIRIAM
creator: BioModels.net / COMBINE
description: MIRIAM is a set of minimum-information guidelines for encoding and annotating quantitative biochemical models. It requires models to be reproducible, attributed and annotated with references to external database resources, which encourages reusable, well-documented computational models (for example in BioModels).

name: Minimum Information Table for the Safety of Engineered Nanomaterials
label: MIT Nanosafety
creator: Leibniz institutes (INM, IUF, IfADo, IWT, FIZ Karlsruhe)
description: A modular minimum information table that sets out what to report with experimental results on the biological effects of engineered nanomaterials. Its six modules are general information, material, biological model, exposure, endpoint read-out, and analysis and statistics. It supports structured, harmonised documentation of nanosafety studies so the data can be reused.

name: Nanomaterial physicochemical data integrated with AOP knowledge in RDF
label: nano-AOP RDF
aliases: nano-AOP RDF; vanrijn2024; From papers to RDF-based integration of physicochemical data and adverse outcome pathways for nanomaterials
creator: Maastricht University (BiGCaT)
description: An RDF knowledge graph that combines literature-curated physicochemical data on nanomaterials with AOP information from the AOP-Wiki, using ontology terms and European Registry of Materials identifiers. A public SPARQL endpoint supports federated queries that relate nanomaterial properties to molecular initiating events and key events.

name: NanoCommons Knowledge Base
label: NanoCommons Knowledge Base
creator: NanoCommons consortium (Biomax Informatics)
description: A knowledge base built in the H2020 NanoCommons project on Biomax's BioXM platform. It brings together nanomaterial characterisation, exposure and (eco)toxicity data from projects and the literature, and offers harmonised, ontology-annotated access to these nanosafety data with analysis tools.

name: Nanopublication
label: Nanopublication
creator: Concept Web Alliance / NBIC
description: A nanopublication is the smallest publishable unit of information: a single assertion in RDF, packaged with named graphs that hold its provenance and publication metadata. Nanopublications get resolvable, verifiable identifiers and are spread over a decentralised server network, so machines can find, cite and reuse individual statements such as AOP or FIP declarations.

name: NORMAN Substance Database
label: NORMAN Substance Database
creator: NORMAN Association
description: Merged and curated database of more than 100,000 substances of environmental concern, compiled from the suspect lists contributed to the NORMAN Suspect List Exchange. It adds harmonised identifiers (CAS, SMILES, InChIKey, PubChem CID, DTXSID), MS-ready structures and predicted properties and ecotoxicity thresholds. It supports suspect and non-target screening, prioritisation and exposure assessment of emerging contaminants.

name: Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI)
label: OBI
creator: OBI Consortium
description: The Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI) is an OBO Foundry ontology of terms for describing biomedical investigations: study designs, protocols, instruments, materials, assays and data transformations. It supports consistent, machine-readable annotation of experimental metadata.

name: OBO Foundry ontologies
label: OBO Foundry ontologies
creator: OBO Foundry
description: A community registry of open, interoperable biomedical ontologies developed under shared principles such as open licences, common formats, unique identifiers and clearly bounded scope. It provides ontology metadata, persistent URLs and quality checks, so data can be annotated with reusable terms that work together across ontologies.

name: OECD Existing Chemicals Database
label: OECD Existing Chemicals Database
creator: OECD
description: OECD database that tracks the chemicals in the OECD Cooperative Chemicals Assessment Programme (formerly the HPV Chemicals Programme). It shows each chemical's assessment status, sponsoring countries, SIDS contacts and categories, and gives access to the published assessment profiles, reports and dossiers.

name: OECD Harmonised Templates (OHTs)
label: OECD harmonized template
creator: OECD
description: Standard data formats, published with XML schemas, for reporting summaries of studies on the physicochemical properties, environmental fate and (eco)toxicological effects of chemicals. Implemented in systems such as IUCLID, they let governments and industry exchange test summary data electronically in one harmonised structure.

name: OMEX (COMBINE archive format)
label: OMEX
creator: COMBINE
description: OMEX (the COMBINE archive format) is a ZIP-based container with a manifest that packs all files of a modelling project (models, simulation descriptions, data and metadata) into one exchangeable file. It lets computational models and their simulation experiments be shared and reproduced as a single package.

name: OECD Omics Reporting Framework (OORF)
label: OORF
stakeholders: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
creator: OECD
description: An OECD reporting framework that sets out what to report for transcriptomics and metabolomics data from laboratory toxicology studies, from study design and data acquisition to processing and statistical analysis. It makes omics data transparent and reproducible enough for regulators to evaluate and use.

name: EFSA OpenFoodTox
label: EFSA OpenFoodTox
creator: EFSA
description: EFSA's open chemical hazards database. For each substance it summarises the identity, the EFSA outputs and legal background, and the critical endpoints, reference points and health-based guidance values from EFSA risk assessments. It is released as downloadable open data and dashboards (built on IUCLID since OpenFoodTox 3.0 in 2026), so the hazard data can be reused, for example in QSAR and read-across work.

name: OpenRiskNet e-infrastructure
label: OpenRiskNet e-infrastructure
creator: OpenRiskNet consortium
description: The OpenRiskNet e-infrastructure offered virtual research environments where containerised data and modelling services for predictive toxicology and risk assessment could be discovered, combined and deployed. The services had documented APIs and semantic annotation, and environments could run on workstations or on public and in-house clouds.

name: OpenTox data model (API)
label: OpenTox data model (API)
creator: OpenTox consortium (Douglas Connect)
description: The web-service API and data model of the OpenTox framework, defining REST interfaces and RDF/OWL representations for compounds, datasets, features, algorithms, models and validation in predictive toxicology. It enabled interoperable, distributed toxicity prediction services and was later reused and extended for nanomaterials by eNanoMapper.

name: OWL (Web Ontology Language)
label: OWL (Web Ontology Language)
creator: W3C
description: The W3C Web Ontology Language, used to write ontologies with formal, logic-based meaning that software can reason over; it is layered on RDF. Most biomedical ontologies, including the eNanoMapper ontology and other ontologies used in toxicology, are built and shared in OWL, which makes annotations semantically interoperable.

name: PARC Toxicology FAIR Implementation Profile
label: PARC Toxicology FIP
aliases: PARC Toxicology FIP; Toxicology specific FIPs (PARC)
creator: PARC (Chemicals Toxicology Community)
description: This is the FAIR Implementation Profile of the PARC Chemicals Toxicology Community. It declares which FAIR-enabling resources the community uses for each FAIR principle and is published as machine-readable nanopublications from the FIP Wizard.

name: PARC exchange standard for FAIR PBK models
label: PARC exchange standard for FAIR PBK…
aliases: An exchange standard for FAIR PBK models in chemical risk assessment
creator: PARC (European Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals)
description: A community exchange standard, developed within PARC, for encoding and annotating physiologically based kinetic (PBK) models used in chemical risk assessment, building on the SBML model format. It lets PBK models be shared, understood and reused across software tools in line with the FAIR principles.

name: INERIS - Chemical Substances Portal
label: INERIS - Chemical Substances Portal
creator: INERIS (French National Institute for Industrial Environment and Risks)
description: French INERIS portal that brings together toxicological, ecotoxicological, physico-chemical, technical-economic and regulatory information on chemical substances. It includes INERIS toxicological and environmental data sheets, acute toxicity thresholds for accidents and environmental quality standards, mainly in French.

name: Protein Ontology (PRO)
label: Protein Ontology (PRO)
creator: PRO Consortium (Protein Information Resource: Georgetown University / University of Delaware)
description: The Protein Ontology (PRO) is an ontology of protein entities, from families to gene-specific forms, isoforms, post-translationally modified forms and complexes, each with a stable identifier. It allows precise annotation of the exact protein form involved, for instance in pathway or key-event descriptions.

name: PubChem
label: PubChem
subdomains: in vitro toxicology; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: NCBI, US National Library of Medicine (NIH)
description: Open chemistry database of the US National Library of Medicine. Its linked Substance, Compound and BioAssay records, contributed by hundreds of depositors, cover structures, identifiers, properties, bioactivity screening results (including Tox21), safety and toxicity information, patents and literature, with web and programmatic access. It is a central hub for chemical identifiers and data in toxicology.

name: QSAR DataBase
label: QSAR DataBase
creator: University of Tartu (Institute of Chemistry)
description: Open repository of (Q)SAR and QSPR models and their data, stored in the open QsarDB format with persistent handles. Published models can be archived, cited, inspected, visualised and re-run for new predictions, which makes in silico models reusable.

name: RDF (Resource Description Framework)
label: RDF (Resource Description Framework)
creator: W3C
description: The W3C Resource Description Framework is a graph data model that states facts as subject-predicate-object triples named by IRIs. It underlies linked data, so toxicology resources such as AOP-Wiki RDF and AOP-DB can be merged with other data and queried across sources.

name: RDMkit
label: RDMkit
creator: ELIXIR
description: ELIXIR's open, community-written toolkit of research data management guidance for the life sciences, organised by data life-cycle stage, role and scientific domain, with links to relevant tools and standards. It helps researchers and data stewards choose the practices, metadata standards and repositories that make data FAIR.

name: RDMkit toxicology page
label: RDMkit toxicology page
subdomains: in vitro toxicology; eco-toxicology; regulatory toxicology
creator: ELIXIR Toxicology Community
description: This is the toxicology domain page of the ELIXIR RDMkit. It explains data management problems and solutions for in vitro, animal, human and ecotoxicology data, and points to relevant standards, databases and tools; its resource list is mirrored as a FAIRsharing collection.

name: FAIR Cookbook recipe: Annotating AOP Key Events with ontology terms
label: FAIR Cookbook recipe: Annotating AOP…
creator: ELIXIR Toxicology Community (INTOXICOM)
description: A FAIR Cookbook recipe, proposed on GitHub and not yet published, on annotating AOP-Wiki key events with ontology terms for process, object, action, cell type and organ, so that key event annotations are consistent and AOPs more interoperable.

name: FAIR Cookbook recipe: Metadata for cell-based assays using Bioassay Ontology (BAO)
label: FAIR Cookbook recipe: Metadata…
creator: ELIXIR Toxicology Community (INTOXICOM)
description: A FAIR Cookbook recipe, proposed on GitHub and not yet published, setting out minimum and desirable metadata for cell-based toxicology assays and how to annotate them with BioAssay Ontology terms, so that the data can be found and linked to AOPs.

name: R-ODAF (Omics Data Analysis Framework for Regulatory application)
label: R-ODAF
aliases: R-ODAF; omics data analysis framework for regulatory application
creator: Maastricht University; Health Canada (Cefic LRI C4 project)
description: R-ODAF is an open-source pipeline with extra filtering criteria that turns raw transcriptomics data (RNA-seq, TempO-Seq, microarray) into reproducible lists of differentially expressed genes. It was designed so that omics data can be accepted in regulatory hazard assessment.

name: S2CIE (semantic, syntactic, and context-based information extraction)
label: S2CIE
creator: Universitat Rovira i Virgili (IISPV)
description: S2CIE is a web platform and API that annotates PubMed abstracts word by word with grammar, entity types and dependencies. It supports rule-based and semantic searches to extract mechanistic evidence, such as stressor-event links and key event relationships, for AOP development.

name: Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML)
label: SBML
creator: SBML community (COMBINE); originated at Caltech (ERATO Kitano project)
description: The Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML) is an XML exchange format for computational models of biological processes, such as biochemical reaction networks. It lets models be shared, reused and simulated across many software tools.

name: SciRAP (Science in Risk Assessment and Policy)
label: SciRAP
subdomains: in vitro toxicology; eco-toxicology; regulatory toxicology
creator: Karolinska Institutet; Stockholm University
description: A web resource from Karolinska Institutet and Stockholm University. It offers criteria and tools for evaluating the reliability and relevance of in vivo, in vitro, ecotoxicity (CRED) and epidemiological studies, plus reporting checklists for researchers. It makes study evaluations transparent and helps academic studies report what regulatory risk assessment needs.

name: SED-ML (Simulation Experiment Description Markup Language)
label: SED-ML
creator: SED-ML community (COMBINE); initiated at EMBL-EBI
description: SED-ML is an XML format for describing simulation experiments on computational models: which models to use, how to change them, which simulations to run and which outputs to produce. It makes model-based simulation results reproducible across software tools.

name: SEND (Standard for Exchange of Nonclinical Data)
label: SEND
stakeholders: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
creator: CDISC
description: A CDISC standard that specifies how data from nonclinical (animal) toxicology studies are organised, formatted and coded for exchange and electronic submission to regulators such as the US FDA. Its implementation guides define domains, variables and controlled terminology so study data can be reviewed, pooled and reused consistently.

name: Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry Specification Format
label: SMILES
creator: David Weininger (US EPA Duluth) and Daylight Chemical Information Systems; OpenSMILES by the Blue Obelisk community
description: Line notation that writes a chemical structure as a short ASCII string, with canonical and isomeric forms and an open community specification (OpenSMILES). It is used to exchange, store and search structures and as input to QSAR, read-across and other in silico toxicology tools.

name: SPARQL
label: SPARQL
creator: W3C
description: The W3C query language and protocol for RDF data. Through SPARQL endpoints, people and software can query and combine linked datasets, such as AOP-Wiki RDF and AOP-DB RDF, in a standard way.

name: Substances in Preparations In the Nordic countries SPIN
label: SPIN
creator: Nordic Council of Ministers (Chemicals Group) with the product registers of Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Finland
description: Public database on the use of chemical substances in products in Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Finland. It is derived from the national product registers without disclosing confidential information and gives tonnages, numbers of products, industry sectors (NACE) and use categories per substance and year, online and as a downloadable offline database. It supports exposure assessment and regulatory prioritisation of chemicals.

name: Toxin and Toxin Target Database
label: T3DB
creator: University of Alberta (Wishart group)
description: Bioinformatics knowledgebase of common toxic substances, such as pollutants, pesticides, drugs and food toxins. Each toxin record links to its protein targets, mechanisms of action, toxicity values, and chemical and spectral data, and can be searched by text, structure or sequence. It was later presented as the Toxic Exposome Database.

name: Tox Biology Checklist
label: Tox Biology Checklist
stakeholders: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
creator: NIEHS-led working group (with US EPA and US FDA NCTR)
description: A checklist of the information that should accompany data from a toxicology or toxicogenomics study: subject characteristics, treatment and sample collection, husbandry and disposition, and the study timeline. It was proposed so that study data deposited in databases such as CEBS could be interpreted and compared across studies. It is no longer maintained.

name: TeMOwl
label: TeMOwl
creator: Fraunhofer SCAI
description: TeMOwl is a Fraunhofer SCAI API service that gives one programmatic access point to controlled vocabularies, terminologies and ontologies from different providers, and maps equivalent concepts across them. In OpenRiskNet it was used to map identifiers and names to concepts.

name: Open Toxicogenomics Project-Genomics Assisted Toxicity Evaluation system
label: Open TG-GATEs
stakeholders: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
creator: Japanese Toxicogenomics Project (NIBIO/NIBIOHN, NIHS and 15 pharmaceutical companies)
description: Toxicogenomics database from the Japanese Toxicogenomics Project with microarray gene expression, blood chemistry, haematology and pathology data for 170 compounds, tested in rats and in rat and human primary hepatocytes. It could be searched by compound or pathological finding, with raw CEL files for download. The original site has closed; the data remain in the Japanese Life Science Database Archive.

name: ELIXIR Toxicology FAIRsharing collection
label: ELIXIR Toxicology collection
creator: ELIXIR Toxicology Community
description: This FAIRsharing collection, curated by the ELIXIR Toxicology Community, groups standards, databases and policies relevant to toxicology and chemical risk assessment, making them easier to find, compare and reuse.

name: Toxicology Data Markup Language
label: ToxML
creator: Leadscope; Lhasa Limited
description: An open XML schema with a controlled vocabulary for recording toxicity studies and endpoints (e.g. genetic toxicity, carcinogenicity, repeated-dose toxicity) in enough detail for database integration and (Q)SAR modelling. Leadscope developed it and Lhasa Limited later hosted it; it gave toxicity data from different sources a common exchange structure. Its website is no longer online.

name: ToxRTool (Toxicological data Reliability assessment Tool)
label: ToxRTool
creator: EC JRC (ECVAM); FoBiG
description: An Excel-based tool, made in an ECVAM-funded project, with criteria for judging the reliability of in vivo and in vitro toxicity studies and assigning them to Klimisch categories 1 to 3. It makes reliability judgements explicit and harmonised, which supports reuse of published and non-guideline studies in regulatory assessment.

name: ToxTemp
label: ToxTemp
creator: University of Konstanz (EU-ToxRisk)
description: A structured template, developed within EU-ToxRisk and aligned with OECD GD 211, for describing cell-based toxicological test methods comprehensively and in a standard order. It captures the metadata needed to judge the readiness, relevance and reliability of in vitro methods and their data for regulatory use.

name: UniProt
label: UniProt
creator: UniProt Consortium (EMBL-EBI, SIB, PIR)
description: A comprehensive, freely available resource of protein sequences and functional information. It combines the expert-curated Swiss-Prot and the automatically annotated TrEMBL sections with the UniRef clusters and the UniParc archive. Its stable accessions and many cross-references are used to identify proteins unambiguously when annotating models, pathways and mechanistic toxicology data.

name: WikiPathways
label: WikiPathways
creator: Gladstone Institutes / Maastricht University (BiGCaT)
description: An open, community-curated database of biological pathways, edited collaboratively and released under CC0 in machine-readable formats such as GPML and RDF. Pathway elements are linked to gene, protein and metabolite identifiers, so the pathways support omics enrichment analysis and links to adverse outcome pathways.
